description: Nigeria's health minister has stated there are about 300,000 health professionals in the country across all cadres, with 85,000-90,000 registered doctors but only 55,000 licensed and practising in-country.
energy_note: Ninety thousand doctors on the register. Fifty-five thousand in the country.

aspect: What that means at the point of care
description: Remaining practitioners face overwork and burnout, hospitals lack specialists in surgery, anaesthesia and paediatrics, and some rural communities have no doctor at all.
energy_note: A community with no doctor, as an ordinary fact.

description: Without broad insurance coverage, treatment is bought at the point of need in cash, which means the sequence is: fall ill, find money, then be treated - and the finding-money step is where people die.

aspect: Which makes illness a household financial event
description: Assets sold, loans taken, school fees diverted. A single serious diagnosis can reset a family's economic position permanently.
energy_note: One diagnosis, and the family is poor again.

description: Her father is admitted at 21:00. The ward will not begin until N180,000 is paid. She calls four people between 21:00 and 01:40 and raises N145,000. The remaining N35,000 arrives at 07:15 from her brother in Ontario.
energy_note: Ten hours of phone calls, standing in a corridor.
